summary: The core is split up by chip: one 007121 module used twice with its tilemap, sprite, interrupt and PROM-lookup logic inside, a palette mixer, a 007452 math block, and the address decoders. MAME's split is different: its driver owns the tilemaps through tile_info callbacks and composes the screen with layered draw calls and a priority bitmap. Where MAME uses arithmetic or draw ordering, the core uses gate equations and AND-gated bank lines (layer priority, tile banking via vreg, the 7-bit multiplier input). The scanline tile and sprite engines are ordinary FPGA line-buffer state machines and do not point either way.

findings.signal: priority as gate equations, not layer draw order
findings.note: Combat School priority is a small NAND/NOR network over each pixel's blank flags, the tile/obj bit and prio_latch, choosing one of the two 007121 outputs. MAME instead switches between two orders of opaque/category tilemap draws and prio_transmask sprite passes.

findings.signal: video bank as AND-gated ROM address lines
findings.note: vreg nibbles are ANDed with one fetched address bit (gfx_pre[14]) to drive ROM lines 17:14. MAME computes bank = 4*((vreg&0xf)-1), clamps it at 0, and forces bank 0 when (attr&0xb0)==0. The core has no trace of that arithmetic.

findings.signal: tilemap logic lives inside the chip module
findings.mame_ref: k007121.cpp (TODO: move tilemaps into device); combatsc_v.cpp:video_start
findings.note: Tile code bits 9-12 come from a per-bit mux driven by mmr[4]/mmr[5] (extra_mask/extra_bits/codeN_sel), inside the 007121 module. MAME's device does not render tilemaps at all; its driver builds three tilemap objects through callbacks.

findings.signal: 007121 outputs a 7-bit colour code after per-chip PROM lookup
findings.note: Each gfx instance runs its tile and object pixels through its own 256x4 PROMs (vprom/oprom), picks tile or sprite per pixel (scr_sel), and outputs {pal_bank, tile/obj, 4-bit} on pxl_out. MAME instead precomputes an indirect pen table from a clut switch over pal 0-7.

findings.signal: palette RAM read twice per pixel
findings.note: The palette address is {gfx_mux, pal_half}, and pal_half toggles at twice the pixel clock, so the two colour bytes are read one after the other and shifted into a 15-bit word. That is how a byte-wide palette RAM gets scanned, not a pen lookup.

The multiplier latches only din[6:0] for factor A, while MAME multiplies two full bytes. Division is a 16-step restoring shift-subtract, with remainder preloaded from the dividend on write. MAME uses / and % with a special case for divide-by-zero. The width difference comes from outside MAME. (The iterative divide by itself is neutral FPGA serialization.)

findings.signal: sprite tile index from address bits, not offset tables
findings.note: Sub-tile code bits code[3:0] come straight from vsub[4:3], hflip, and a counter that increments {code[2],code[0],h4}. MAME adds entries from its x_offset {0,1,4,5} and y_offset {0,2,8,10} tables. The list ends on scan_base<0x13b, 384 pixels, or y==240, not MAME's 264-block rule.

NMI fires on rising edges of vdump[4] or vdump[5], chosen by mmr[7][4]; IRQ fires on LVBL falling; FIRQ comes from a toggle flip-flop clocked by IRQ release. MAME uses a 16-line timer callback with a mask test and fires IRQ/FIRQ at scanline 240.

I/O selects come from A[15:9] and then A[4:2], with A[5] as a gate and A[1:0] ignored, so the selects mirror the way an incomplete decode would. Strobe names (sdata_cs, son_cs, dmp_cs, bank_en) are not MAME's handler names (sh_irqtrigger_w, bankselect_w). The decoded addresses themselves are shared with MAME, so they are neutral.

findings.signal: scanline tile/sprite engines into BRAM line buffers
findings.note: A per-line state machine fetches 16-bit words from SDRAM and writes 4 pixels into a line buffer. This is standard FPGA scheduling: it does not reproduce MAME's frame draw order, and it does not follow the chip's own fetch timing either.

findings.signal: register bit semantics and memory map
findings.note: The MMR bit assignments, ROM banking ({bank[3:1]} vs 8+bit0), and the sound map at 8000-E000 match MAME. Any correct core must share these.
